Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the productive call this week. Per our discussion, I put together a proposal that tries to balance Nebula's desire for predictable economics with flexibility for your product teams as usage ramps. High-level summary attached (NB-3784_proposal_commit_lattice_v2.pdf):

- Structure: 2-year committed contract built as a "commit lattice" — Year 1 base commit + Year 2 tranche that can be released in H2 if uptake meets agreed triggers.
- Billing: annual invoicing with an optional quarterly true-up window (see section 2).
- Uptake contingency: a defined "escape" that gives Nebula an ability to reduce Year 2 tranche up to 35% within the first 90 days of Year 2 if actual usage falls below threshold X.
- Auto-renew: opt-in auto-renew at Year 2 with a capped uplift; we can keep a co-term option if you want all products aligned to a single renewal date.
- Onboarding & burst: reserved burst pool included for first 60 days; additional burst capacity can be purchased at a predictable uplift rate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick alignment call to confirm the triggers and tolerance bands (30 min)
2) Send a one-page with the billing cadence and signature-ready DocuSign
3) Loop in procurement/legal for a single redline pass if acceptable

Attached: NB-3784_proposal_commit_lattice_v2.pdf (detailed), NB-3784_onepage_summary.pdf (executive one-pager).

If these elements look ok, can we lock a time for Mon/Tue next week for the trigger alignment?

Thanks —
Rishi

Yes — we can invoice quarterly. No change to the committed discount (Year 1 baseline retains the 18% discount). Quarterly invoices will reflect the committed amount amortized across quarters with a quarterly reconciliation true-up. Payment terms remain Net 30.

> 2) Co-terming — we currently have two Redwood products on different dates. We'd prefer co-terming all products onto our fiscal 07/01 boundary if possible. Will that require an amendment to Year 1 billing?

We've included a pro-rated bridge in the attached packet (DocuSign_Nebula_Renewal_0615.pdf). The bridge prorates remaining days in the current period and combines into a single 07/01 renewal boundary. No retroactive charges beyond the pro-rate.

> 3) The escape hatch sounds reasonable; who will own the usage measurement and sign-off for the triggers? We need a process that doesn't require weekly syncs.

Process recommended: Redwood will produce a monthly usage report; quarterly true-up windows are the formal reconciliation points. If a trigger dispute arises, Nebula has 10 business days from delivery of the quarterly report to raise a dispute with evidence; otherwise the report stands. We will add a short SLA for turnaround on disputed items (Redwood responds within 5 business days).
